messages.subject: RE: Plotting nondetects and detected value with confidence interval
parts:
How about this? I am trying to create a similar plot as yours with basic graphics…

 

mydata <- read.csv("http://doylesdartden.com/Example-ND.csv", sep=",")

 

mydata$EMDF <- ifelse(mydata$D_EMD==1, "Detected", "NonDetect")

 

ggplot(data = mydata, aes(x=Year, y=EMD, col=EMDF)) +

geom_point(aes(shape=EMDF)) +

geom_smooth(span=2)+ 

scale_colour_manual(values=c("black","red")) +

theme(legend.position=c(0.2,0.9))

ggtitle("Locally Weighted Scatterplot Smoothing Curve")

 

--Kaori

 

From: ggp...@googlegroups.com [mailto:ggp...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of KyDavidDoyle
Sent: Monday, April 22, 2013 10:18 PM
To: ggp...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Plotting nondetects and detected value with confidence interval

 

Hello Everyone,

 

I deal groundwater data.  One thing I have to deal with is that often I have results that are non-detect at the laboratory reporting limit so I like to plot them in a different color or marker.  I also often use LOESS smoothing curves to show the general trend.  To that end, I use the code below to plot my graphs.

 

I would like to be able plot the same but with a confidence interval around it.  I can do it with this code but I don't know how to do the non-detects vs. the detects.  Any suggestions?

 

Thanks

David

 

mydata <- read.csv("http://doylesdartden.com/Example-ND.csv", sep=",")

qplot(Year, EMD, data = mydata, geom = c("point", "smooth"),span = 1)

 

 

 

 

# my normal code but no confidence intervals

mydata <- read.csv("http://doylesdartden.com/Example-ND.csv", sep=",")

attach(mydata)

reg1 <- lm(EMD~Year)

par(cex=1)

 

#Plots the data but makes nondetects a different color and type based on column D_EMD being a 0 for ND and 1 for detect.

plot(Year, EMD, col=ifelse(D_EMD, "black", "red"),ylab = "EMD", pch=ifelse(D_EMD, 19, 17), cex = 0.7)

  

# Apply loess smoothing using the default span value of 0.8.  You can change the curve by changing the span value.

y.loess <- loess(y ~ x, span=0.8, data.frame(x=Year, y=EMD))

 

# Compute loess smoothed values for all points along the curve

y.predict <- predict(y.loess, data.frame(x=Year))

 

# Plots the curve.

lines(Year,y.predict)

 

#Add Legend to graph.  You can change the size of the box by changing cex = 0.75  Large # makes it larger.

legend("topleft", c("Smoothing Curve", "Detected", "NonDetect"), col = c(1, "black","red"), cex = 0.75,

       text.col = "black", lty = c(1 ,-1, -1), pch = c(-1, 19, 17),

       merge = TRUE, bg = 'gray90')

 

#Add title

title(main="Locally Weighted Scatterplot Smoothing Curve")

 

# Done

--
